What nobody revisited is the DUTY whose last step is `git add` + commit + **push**, and whose sentence still reads *"origin IS the offsite copy"*.** ✅ **NOTHING IS LOST, ESTABLISHED NOT ASSUMED: the series survives INTACT in the preserved pre-swap clone `Gold Rush-history-local` — **28 TRACKED mirrors `2026-08-24` → `2026-09-20`**, today's included, pulled `02:44:44Z` inside F-2601-1's randomized `[02:00,03:00)Z` window (control: `39,673` tracked files there). AND IT IS GENUINELY OFFSITE rather than disk-local: **`146` remote-tracking refs hold the path**, among them `origin/main` (**28** paths = `GoldRush-history`) and `archive/main` (**27** paths = `GoldRush-archive`); control `742` remote-tracking refs. ⓘ Remote-tracking refs can be STALE (F-2563-1) so that is evidence about the last fetch, labelled as such; the disk copy is measured directly.** ⛔ **AND THE PARAGRAPH THAT STOOD HERE IS RETRACTED BY ITS OWN SUCCESSOR-CHECK — RESTATED, NOT DELETED, BECAUSE THE ERROR IS THE INSTRUCTIVE HALF: I wrote that `artifacts/ledger-backups/` sits on NEITHER the A3 HEAD re-add list NOR the swap checklist's disk-local list and concluded *"an omission in a measured plan, not a decision"*, inferring it from the series being under 30 days old and therefore inside the 60-day re-add window. **THAT INFERENCE IS WRONG AND F-2661-1 MEASURED THE OPPOSITE SIX FIRES EARLIER: the A3 shrink dropped the path DELIBERATELY, classified as a `"user-data backup"`.** My own evidence never distinguished the two readings — an absent path looks identical whether it was forgotten or excluded on purpose — so I read a silence as an oversight. ⓘ **AND THE WHOLE FINDING IS LARGELY A DUPLICATE, WHICH IS WORSE THAN BEING WRONG AND IS SAID PLAINLY: F-2661-1 (measured s2661, re-verified s2662) already carries the PUBLIC-origin hazard, the ENOENT/`ls-files 0`/no-gitignore measurements three ways, the existential-discharge-test direction, the private-archive recommendation, the `do NOT pull and do NOT commit` binding, and even the reusable half (*"a duty's safety can be a property of its DESTINATION rather than of its content … when a repo's visibility changes, re-read every standing duty that ends in `push`"*). F-1600-1 prices duplicate reporting to the owner as WORSE than doing nothing, and I reached the desk's own conclusion independently only because I had not yet read the desk I was about to carry.** ➡️ **SO WHAT SURVIVES AS THIS FIRE'S OWN CONTRIBUTION IS NARROW AND IS THE ONLY PART TO CITE: (1) **THE SITE.** F-2661-1's binding instruction lived in `tasks/BACKLOG.md` and on the OWNER'S DESK — the two surfaces F-1654-1 proved a fire does NOT read at decision time — and `scripts/fire.md`'s LB-01 duty, the surface a fire reads AT THE MOMENT IT APPLIES, carried NO stop at all until this clause. That is this factory's most-repeated finding (F-2153-1 · F-2204-1 · F-2350-1 · F-2360-1 · F-2365-1 · F-2403-1 · F-2414-1 · F-2436-1 · F-2449-1 · F-2451-1): a cure with no reader. (2) **THE VACUOUS GATE.** F-2661-1 records the account-class defence as *"INTACT … refuses loudly on account-class rows"*, which is TRUE and INCOMPLETE: on an ABSENT corpus `ledger-mirror-exposure.mjs` does not refuse, it prints `✅ CLEAN`, so the gate standing in front of this door clears on an empty room. (3) F-2667-3, the retention ref-space, which nothing on the desk covers.** 💡 **THE REUSABLE HALF IS THEREFORE NOT THE ONE I FIRST WROTE, AND IT IS SHARPER: **READ THE DESK YOU ARE ABOUT TO CARRY BEFORE YOU SPEND A FIRE MEASURING.** The desk segment is extracted verbatim at HANDOFF time, which is the END of a fire — so a fire that investigates first and carries the desk last can re-derive a standing item in full, at full cost, and file it as new. Six fires and one owner recommendation already stood behind mine. **Grep the desk and `tasks/BACKLOG.md` for your subject BEFORE the first measurement, not after the last one** — and when a predecessor's finding says DELIBERATE and your inference says OVERSIGHT, the predecessor measured and you inferred. ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: REALISED COST ZERO — no fire has pulled since the swap, so nothing was ever committed or pushed here; the series is whole; today's mirror exists; and `ledger-mirror-freshness` REFUSES correctly and LOUDLY (`⛔ CANNOT VERIFY … Nothing was measured.`), exactly as F-2662-1 predicted for it. NOT a false green about the series.** 🎯 **WHAT EARNS A STOP IS THE DIRECTION THROUGH A ONE-WAY DOOR (F-2353-2: force-push is deny-listed, so a published row is not retractable). The duty's prose discharge test is *"does the directory hold today's file?"* — ENOENT reads as **NOT DISCHARGED, RUN THE PULL** — and `ledger-backup-pull.mjs`'s `DEFAULT_DEST` is anchored to `import.meta.url`, so the pull `mkdir`s the series straight into the PUBLIC repo's working tree. Then the one instrument whose entire job is to stand in front of that door says yes: `ledger-mirror-exposure.mjs` on the absent corpus prints **`✅ CLEAN — no mirror directory here, so there is nothing to expose.`** — F-2662-1's vacuous-bucket shape on a THIRD tool.** ⓘ **THE MITIGATION IS NAMED AND IT IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS: that instrument is a leg of `test:ledger-guards`, run at a fire's LAST act, so it WOULD see a post-pull mirror — but it refuses only on ACCOUNT-class rows, and there are none today (sign-in is down, F-MAIL-0829). So a plaintext county database pushed to a public repository is **GREEN by every gate this factory owns**, and the clause below it — *"a plaintext ledger of county standings is fine"*, a judgement taken while origin was PRIVATE — would tell the fire it was right.** ➡️ **BINDING UNTIL THE OWNER RULES, landed at the site in `scripts/fire.md` §LB-01: DO NOT pull, DO NOT `git add` a mirror, DO NOT push one. LB-01 is PARKED, not failing; the series needs no rescue and the droplet keeps its own 14-day window on top.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is measured rather than lazy: the mechanical key is *"is origin public?"*, and a PUBLIC origin is now the LAWFUL, permanent, owner-ruled state of this repository — a red there fires on every correct run forever and is excused into uselessness inside a week (F-1460-1, the `cross-engine` fate). Both instruments are already correct: one REFUSES, the other DECLARES its absent corpus. What was missing is the READER's instruction, which is now at the site.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is a NEW AXIS after *an mtime records a DELETION* (F-2607-1), *a refusal is a bucket* (F-2617-1), *a registry is mutable* (F-2636-1) and *a corpus can be REPLACED* (F-2662-1): all of those ask whether an instrument can still SEE its corpus. **HERE THE INSTRUMENT CORRECTLY SAYS IT CANNOT, AND THE DUTY'S NEXT STEP WOULD RE-CREATE THE CORPUS SOMEWHERE THAT WRITING MEANS SOMETHING ELSE.** A repository swap moves the FLOOR an instrument stands on and it also moves the WALLS: the same `git push` is a BACKUP in a private repo and a PUBLICATION in a public one — identical syntax, identical exit code, no warning anywhere. **When a repository is replaced, re-ask not only "can my instruments still read this?" but "does WRITING here still mean what it meant?" — and audit every standing duty whose last step is a push.**

🪢 **F-2664-1 — CONTENTION IS A *STATE*, NOT AN EVENT, SO IT CANNOT BE READ OFF A DELTA — F-2663-1'S BINDING PRE-DRAIN READ WENT BLIND ONE FIRE AFTER IT LANDED, IN EXACTLY THE SCENARIO IT PREDICTED (measured and cured s2664).** F-2663-1 made it binding to run `worktree-registry-ledger` before any drain and *"READ THE ADDED LIST BY NAME"*, because *"an ADDED tree containing your drain is a STOP (§7.6)"*. That is right about the VALUE and wrong about the CHANNEL: **ADDED is a diff against the banked baseline, and F-2636-1's duty tells the SAME fire to re-bank with `--update` in the SAME fire** — so the contending tree enters the baseline within minutes while the contention it represents persists for hours. 📊 **MEASURED s2664, the control asserting its own validity first (F-2215-1 — the tool really ran and really produced output): s2663 banked `7 → 9` INCLUDING `scratchpad/wt-corr2-land`, and my run's WHOLE output was **`310` bytes / `8` lines**, read whole and never `head`ed (F-2606-1), saying `✅ UNCHANGED — the registry set is identical to the banked one (9 paths)` and **naming that tree NOWHERE** (`includes('wt-corr2-land')` → **false**). The tree was holding `4be40ccb2` — `drain: merge sol/map-art-campaign-2 319d3c917`, i.e. MY EXACT CANDIDATE — with its newest FILE mtime **`4.13` min** old (epoch-ms both sides, F-2567-1; `lstat`, symlinks skipped, F-2607-1), and it ADVANCED to `ec59c0957 review: … LANDED` while I measured.** 🎯 **AND IT IS F-2663-1'S OWN PREDICTED COLLISION, ARRIVING ON THE VERY NEXT FIRE: that finding warned *"F-A3-2's gate is TEMPORARY — it clears the instant the store lands on main — and a fire arriving after that reads `drain-block-check` ✅ CLEAR, sees a done-move and a lane 3 ahead, drains, and walks straight into a merge the attended session already has in flight."* **Every one of those conditions was TRUE for me and I measured each: the store is CLEAN on `main` (`068c0db`, gate CLEARED); `drain-block-check` → ✅ CLEAR; `dry-board-probe` → `REAL DRAINS: 1`; lane-c `3` ahead.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost ZERO — I STOOD OFF and nothing collided — and this is NOT a false green about the drain, because `drain-block-check` correctly answers a different question and never claimed otherwise. **But the ONLY reason I looked at that tree is that my predecessor NAMED it in HANDOFF PROSE**, and this factory has twice established that prose is the wrong channel for a decision-time fact: F-1654-1 proved a fire does not read the handoff surface at decision time, and F-2373-1 proved a handoff instruction is PERISHABLE across the very drain that discharges it. A fire two handoffs later runs the prescribed instrument, gets an all-clear, and drains.** 🛠️ **CURE AT THE SITE, so it cannot rot out of sync with this sentence: an **ALWAYS-ON, BASELINE-INDEPENDENT** `in flight` declaration printed BEFORE every verdict branch — an unconditional COUNT line (a corpus fact whose zero is the all-clear, F-2208-1) plus, gated on the list being non-empty, each tree's PATH · HEAD · branch · containment verdict · SUBJECT, and the STOP rule. **Gated, never always-on as a section: an empty block across a 9-row fleet is the noise that decays a declaration into a formality (F-2366-1).**** 🚦 **IT DECLARES AND DOES NOT REFUSE — exit codes and verdict words are UNTOUCHED (measured: `rc=0` both modes, verdict byte-identical) — and the restraint is INHERITED rather than re-argued: a worktree holding unlanded work is LAWFUL, routine attended work, so a red would fire during ordinary correct operation and be excused into uselessness inside a week (F-1460-1, the `cross-engine` fate). It is the same restraint F-2366-1 took for BUSY and F-2638-1 took for this very tool.** 🔑 **CONTAINMENT IS ASKED **BY VALUE** (`rev-list --count <main>..<head>`), NEVER BY `merge-base --is-ancestor`, and that is a measured choice rather than a style one: F-2561-1 established that `--is-ancestor` uses exit 1 as a legitimate VERDICT and that the *"exit 1 with empty stderr"* discriminator is UNAVAILABLE through a wrapper collapsing failure to `err.message` (node supplies *"Command failed:"*), which in that fire misfiled THREE genuinely-ahead trees as unanswerable. A count has no overloaded exit code.** 🔒 **Guarded by `6` NEW ARMS on the EXISTING guard (F-1261-1 — a second guard here is the sprawl this file warns about); `scripts/worktree-registry-ledger-guard.test.mjs` now carries `20`, all green, rooted in `test:ledger-guards`.** 🔬 **TEETH, `8` variants manufactured IN PLACE with the subject restored BYTE-IDENTICALLY (sha256-asserted) after every one, and the sweep doubled as a reachability audit: **ALL SIX NEW ARMS red under at least one variant, so none is decoration.** Pre-cure verbatim reds all six · the **POSITION** defect (section gated on the delta — the exact s2664 shape) reds **15,16,18** · unconditional section reds **17** (plus 7, benign over-coverage) · dropping the containment test reds **19 ALONE** · silent-empty on an unverifiable main reds **20 ALONE** · refuse-instead-of-declare reds **18 ALONE**.** ⚠️ **ONE METHOD NOTE PAID FOR AGAIN, AND IT IS F-2617-1'S OWN, WHICH I HAD READ: my first refuse-instead-of-declare variant set `process.exitCode = 1` and **reddened NOTHING** — because this tool ends in `process.exit(0)`, which OVERRIDES `process.exitCode`. I was one step from recording arm 18 as decoration. The variant that targets the actual mechanism (returning a non-zero code FROM the `process.exit()` call) reds it ALONE. **An arm that reds under nothing may be a weak VARIANT rather than a toothless ARM — build the variant that targets the mechanism before you accuse the assertion.**** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is a NEW AXIS after *how WIDE is the selector* (F-2358-1), *can its axis EXPRESS the defect* (F-2389-1), *which TREE* (F-2484-1), *a registry is not a census* (F-2485-1), *entries vs files* (F-2490-1), *an undeclared denominator* (F-2561-1), *which CLOCK* (F-2567-1), *an mtime records a DELETION* (F-2607-1) and *a refusal is a bucket* (F-2617-1): every one of those asks whether a subject set was DRAWN correctly. **THIS ONE IS DRAWN CORRECTLY AND SIGNALLED ON THE WRONG *TENSE*.** A delta reports a TRANSITION; a hazard that persists is a CONDITION; and the two are typographically identical in a tool's output — `ADDED 2` and `ADDED 0` look like more-danger and less-danger when they actually mean *it started* and *it is still happening*. **When you build a signal, ask whether the thing you are signalling is an EVENT or a STATE — and if it is a state, ask what your instrument says on the SECOND fire, after the first one has banked it away.** The sharper half: this cure was ONE FIRE OLD, its author measured it correctly, and it still expired at the first re-bank — because the duty that consumes the signal and the duty that erases it are THE SAME DUTY.
